newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.S.-backed Kurds gather for Iraq evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-backed Kurds gather for Iraq evacuation.

text.p: Hundreds of Kurds who worked for the United States in northern Iraq gathered at the Turkish border on Sunday to begin evacuating the region in fear of the increased influence of President Saddam Hussein, witnesses said.

They said six battered blue-and-white buses, guarded by Iraqi Kurdish guerrillas, brought the Kurds to the Habur border crossing for passage to a camp inside Turkey where they were to be processed for asylum in the United States.

As many as 2,500 Iraqi Kurds were expected to be relocated to a camp in the Turkish town of Silopi. Most worked as employees of U.S. aid programmes and a Western air force that patrols a no-fly zone in northern Iraq. But some are believed to have been engaged in intelligence activities for the Americans.
"I feel great. I just want to get across that bridge," said a refugee who identified himself only as Moyyad. A Turkish tank waited on the other side of the border.

The pro-U.S. Kurds had been holed up in small hotels and private residences waiting to flee since Iraqi troops helped the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) faction take the city of Arbil from a rival group late last month.
The KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, now controls most of northern Iraq.
